chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil ibn Salih from some of our companions from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them): Regarding the woman who marries during her waiting period.

He said: 'They are separated, and she observes one waiting period from them. If she gives birth to a child after six months or more, the child belongs to the latter (husband); and if she gives birth to a child in less than six months, the child belongs to the first (husband).'

key_terms.عِدَّةٌ: Waiting period (Iddah) for a divorced or widowed woman

ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined for a child born to a woman who married twice during her waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *luhq* (lineage attribution) in cases of overlapping marriages, a key topic in Shia jurisprudence regarding the validity of the second union during the first husband's *iddah*. It establishes a six-month gestational benchmark to determine paternity, ensuring that the child is attributed to the husband whose marriage was active at the time of conception or birth, thereby preserving lineage integrity (*thubut al-ansab*).
